content_html:
Lima is a vibrant city, but sometimes we need a break from traffic and routine. Fortunately, the Peruvian capital is surrounded by incredible short getaway destinations, whether you're looking for sun, adventure, or nature. Here we present you the best options for an unforgettable weekend.

1. Southern Beaches: Relax with Sun and Sand

Location: Less than 2 hours south of Lima
Ideal for: Relaxing, surfing and enjoying marine cuisine

If what you are looking for is to disconnect by the sea, the southern beaches of Lima They are the perfect option. Some of the most popular are:

  • Punta Hermosa: Ideal for surfers and lovers of good seafood.
  • Punta Negra and San Bartolo: With a calmer atmosphere, perfect for swimming or walking along the boardwalk.
  • Asia: Famous for its nightlife and exclusive restaurants on Asia Boulevard.
  • Puerto Viejo and Cerro Azul: More remote beaches with a relaxed atmosphere for those looking to completely disconnect.

Tip: If you go in summer, leave early to avoid traffic on the Panamericana Sur.

2. Lunahuaná: Adventure and Wines in the Cañete River Valley

Location: 3 hours south of Lima
Ideal for: Extreme sports and gastronomic tourism

Lunahuaná is the perfect destination for those looking adrenaline and nature. Here you can do:

  • Canoeing on the Cañete River, with rapids ideal for beginners and experts.
  • Mountain biking and canopy, for those who want an extra dose of adventure.
  • Wine and pisco tasting, in traditional vineyards in the area.

Furthermore, the gastronomy in Lunahuaná is unmissable. Don't forget to try a shrimp crackling or one dry soup with carapulcra.

Tip: The best time for canoeing is from December to April, when the river has the greatest flow.

3. Canta y Obrajillo: Nature and Andean Landscapes

Location: 3 hours northeast of Lima
Ideal for: Hiking and natural landscapes

If you prefer mountains and fresh air, Sing and Obrajillo They are excellent options for a short trip. In this area you can:

  • Visit the Obrajillo waterfall, a beautiful waterfall surrounded by vegetation.
  • Enjoy a picnic next to the Chillón River, perfect for a family break.
  • Explore the Chuchún lagoon, a little-known place with stunning views.

Tip: Bring warm clothing, as temperatures can drop quite a bit at night.

4. Paracas and Ballestas Islands: Nature and Marine Wonders

Location: 3 and a half hours south of Lima
Ideal for: Wildlife watching and paradisiacal beaches

Paracas is a spectacular destination where the desert meets the sea. Here you can:

  • Take a boat tour to the Ballestas Islands, where you will see sea lions, Humboldt penguins and exotic birds.
  • Explore the Paracas National Reserve, with unique beaches such as La Mina and Raspón.
  • Enjoy water sports, such as paddle surfing and kitesurfing.

Tip: Bring a windproof jacket for the island tour, as it can get cold on the boat.

5. Marcahuasi: Mystery and Adventure in the Heights

Location: 4 hours east of Lima
Ideal for: Trekking and camping

If you are looking for a unique experience, the Marcahuasi stone amphitheater It is a destination that you cannot miss. This mystical place, located at more than 4,000 meters above sea level, is famous for its gigantic rock formations with human and animal shapes.

To get there, you must take a walk of approximately 3 hours from San Pedro de Casta. The best experience is camping on the plateau and see the starry sky, one of the most impressive in Peru.

Tip: Wear thermal clothing and stay well hydrated to avoid altitude sickness.

These were some places that you can visit on a weekend, remember you can book now.
